Simulate a two-group cohort with controlled depth, heterogeneity, and shift.

Source: R/synthetic-data.R
simulate_composition_cohort.Rd

Each subject draws a latent composition from a Dirichlet centered on its group's mean composition, then draws cells_per_subject counts from a multinomial on that composition. Three knobs separate the sources of variation the sampling vignette studies: cells_per_subject sets count noise within a subject, concentration sets how far subjects scatter around their group mean (larger is more homogeneous), and shift moves composition mass between two categories in the second group only.

Usage

simulate_composition_cohort(
  n_subjects_per_group = 8,
  n_categories = 10,
  cells_per_subject = 2000,
  concentration = 50,
  shift = 0,
  groups = c("Control", "Treatment"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n_subjects_per_group

Subjects per group; length 1 or 2.

n_categories

Number of categories (>= 2).

cells_per_subject

Multinomial count total per subject, typically cells (or events).

concentration

Dirichlet concentration per group; length 1 or 2.

shift

Composition mass moved in the second group, in [0, first category's baseline share).

groups

Two group labels.

seed

Random seed, or NULL to use the current stream.

Value

List with long_table (subjectId, category, group, n), latent_counts (subjects by categories latent compositions scaled to cells_per_subject, for noise-free reference statistics), and group (named factor).

Details

The baseline mean composition decays linearly over categories (e.g. 10 categories run from about 0.18 down to 0.02), so the shift moves shift mass from the first, most abundant category to the last, rarest one.
